# KeyBurn

> Zero-knowledge, self-destructing secret sharing. Secrets are encrypted on the sender's device, the key lives in the link after "#" and never reaches the server, and each secret is deleted after its last view or when it expires.

AI agents: open KeyBurn links with osss, a small command-line tool that runs on the user's computer and gives you a handle instead of the value (setup: https://keyburn.dev/agents.md). Fetching a link without a browser returns step-by-step instructions, never the secret: the key after "#" is never sent to the server. Don't paste links into other services.

## Docs

- [How it works](https://keyburn.dev/security.md): encryption, what the server stores, and the limits of the design
- [For AI agents](https://keyburn.dev/agents.md): the osss CLI and MCP server, which open secret links locally without printing them
- [Agent skill](https://keyburn.dev/.well-known/agent-skills/osss/SKILL.md): rules and steps for an agent handling a secret link
- [Authentication](https://keyburn.dev/auth.md): no accounts or API keys; a link is the capability
- [API description](https://keyburn.dev/openapi.json): OpenAPI 3.1; every value is produced by client-side cryptography

## Pages

- [Share a secret](https://keyburn.dev/index.md): create a self-destructing link in the browser
- [Request a secret](https://keyburn.dev/request.md): ask someone to send you a secret that only you can open
